title: Euler characteristic of a nodal curve from its normalization
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $B$ be a proper reduced connected $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-weil-connected-scheme], nodal at every nonsmooth point in the sense that its completed local rings are $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and let $B_1,\ldots,B_v$ be its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. For each $i$, let $\widetilde B_i\to B_i$ be the normalization [def-sc-normalization], assumed smooth proper connected, and put $g_i=\dim_k H^1(\widetilde B_i,\mathcal O_{\widetilde B_i})$ [def-sc-genus]. Let $e$ be the number of internal nodes of $B$, counting a self-node once. Then, for the Euler characteristic of the structure sheaf [def-pc-euler-characteristic], $$\chi(B)=v-e-\sum_{i=1}^{v}g_i.$$

source.place: Tag 0C1R (lemma-prepare-delta-invariant), normalization exact sequence; curves.tex Tag 0CBW (lemma-split-node), the completed split-node model. Its normalization quotient is k[[u]] direct-sum k[[v]] modulo the pairs with equal constant term, hence one copy of k. Summing normalized-component Euler characteristics gives the formula.

proof.text: Let $\nu:\widetilde B=\coprod_i\widetilde B_i\to B$ be the normalization map. The supporting normalization-quotient lemma [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-quotient] supplies a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_B\to\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde B}\to Q\to0$ of coherent modules and gives $\chi(B,Q)=e$.

First identify each supplied integral closed component with the canonical reduced closed component, using the universal property of a reduced closed subscheme. Transport normalization across these isomorphisms using its universal property [lem-sbc-relative-normalization-universal-property], and reindex the coproduct by the supplied component equivalence. Apply Euler additivity [lem-pc-euler-additive] to Step 1. The coherent terms have finite-dimensional cohomology and a common upper vanishing bound [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined]; finite-pushforward finite presentation and the explicit skyscraper decomposition supply the hypotheses of the Lean additivity API. Since a finite morphism is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], affine cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge], in the numerical form Modules.eulerChar_pushforward_of_isAffineHom, gives chi(B, nu_*O)=chi(tilde B,O). The pairwise-disjoint-open-cover Euler formula Modules.eulerChar_eq_sum_of_pairwise_disjoint_of_isQuasicoherent, followed by isomorphism invariance of cohomology, computes the Euler characteristic of the coproduct as the sum of the component Euler characteristics. Thus chi(B)=sum_i chi(tilde B_i)-e. This uses the already-proved numerical affine API, without invoking the recorded edge-map theorem or a finite-Euler wrapper.

The closed embedding identifies the dimension of each supplied integral component with that of its image. Normalization preserves this dimension [lem-sc-normalization-exists], so every normalized component has dimension one. Smoothness then gives relative dimension one over k. Properness, smoothness and connectedness are supplied in the hypotheses. Apply the existing structure-sheaf specialization of Riemann--Roch, eulerChar_unit_eq [lem-sc-riemann-roch], and identify arithmetic and geometric genus using genus_eq_arithmeticGenus [lem-pc-genus-agrees-sc]. This gives chi(tilde B_i,O)=1-g_i. The global-functions calculation [lem-sc-global-functions] supplies the GlobalSectionsBijective instance required by these formulas. Finiteness of normalization [lem-sc-normalization-exists] also makes the component coproduct proper for Step 2.

proof.text: Substituting the component values into Step 2 yields $\chi(B)=\sum_i(1-g_i)-e=v-e-\sum_{i=1}^v g_i$, as claimed. The formula also counts a self-node once because the supporting quotient lemma has one local quotient copy of $k$ for each singular point.
